exposure: Repeated lumbar punctures prior to ventricular drainage
cohort: Fifty-three preterm neonates born <34 weeks' gestation with intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) and subsequent posthemorrhagic ventricular dilatation (PHVD).
finding: Ventricular decompression resulted in an immediate increase in regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rScO2) in patients who underwent direct ventricular drainage, while those with repeated lumbar punctures prior to drainage consistently maintained higher rScO2 and lower cFTOE levels and showed no additional acute effects from decompression.
followup_time: Observations were taken 2 weeks before and 2 weeks after ventricular decompression, which was performed at a median age of 18 days of life, meaning the last observation was approximately 32 days of life.
